name: STM32F030C8T6
title: STM32F030x4/x6/x8: value-line 48 MHz Cortex-M0 microcontrollers, 16 KB to 64 KB flash, 2.4 V to 3.6 V
summary: A value-line family of 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0 microcontrollers that run to 48 MHz from a 2.4 V to 3.6 V supply. Parts carry 16 KB to 64 KB of flash and 4 KB or 8 KB of parity-checked SRAM, a 12-bit 1 µs ADC, a 5-channel DMA, an advanced motor-control timer and up to six more 16-bit timers, a calendar RTC, and up to two each of I2C, USART and SPI, in TSSOP20, LQFP32, LQFP48 and LQFP64 for -40 °C to 85 °C. The STM32F030C8T6 is the LQFP48 part with 64 KB of flash, 8 KB of SRAM and 39 I/Os.
key_figures: VDD and VDDA 2.4 V to 3.6 V
22 mA typ at 48 MHz from flash, peripherals on (VDD = 3.6 V)
Stop 5 µA typ from VDD (regulator low-power); Standby 2 µA typ from VDD with LSI and IWDG on
12-bit, 1 µs, up to 16 external channels, 0 V to VDDA
HSI 8 MHz, HSI14 14 MHz for the ADC, HSE 4 MHz to 32 MHz, LSI 40 kHz, LSE 32.768 kHz, PLL to 48 MHz
up to 55, up to 36 of them 5 V tolerant; C8T6: 39
up to 2 × I2C (one 1 Mbit/s FM+), 2 × USART (6 Mbit/s), 2 × SPI (18 Mbit/s), SWD

notes: (1) No TIM15.
(2) No SPI2.
(3) No I2C2.
(4) No USART2.

The x4, x6 and x8 groups: STM32F030x4 is the F4; STM32F030x6 the C6 and K6; STM32F030x8 the C8 and R8. TIM6, TIM15, SPI2, USART2 and I2C2 exist on the x8 only. A TR suffix on the order code is tape and reel. The 18 ADC channels of the R8 count the two internal ones (temperature sensor and VREFINT).

CL1 and CL2 are normally equal, 5 pF to 20 pF, high-quality ceramics; REXT is chosen for the crystal. A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces Y1, C1 and C2.

Inside, NRST has a pull-up of about 40 kΩ to VDD, a Schmitt input and a pulse filter. Whatever drives NRST has to pull it below VIL(NRST) max, 0.8 V, or the reset is not seen.

operation.text: Cortex-M0 core to 48 MHz; 16 KB to 64 KB flash and 4 KB to 8 KB SRAM with parity; CRC unit; POR/PDR and Sleep, Stop and Standby; 4 MHz to 32 MHz crystal oscillator, 32 kHz oscillator for the RTC, 8 MHz RC with a x6 PLL option and 40 kHz RC; up to 55 fast I/Os, all able to raise external interrupts, up to 36 of them 5 V tolerant; 5-channel DMA; one 12-bit 1.0 µs ADC with up to 16 channels, converting 0 to 3.6 V from its own 2.4 V to 3.6 V analog supply; up to 10 timers; calendar RTC that can wake the chip from Stop and Standby by alarm or periodically; up to two I2C (one with 1 Mbit/s Fast-mode Plus and 20 mA sink), two USARTs (synchronous SPI master and modem control, one with auto baud) and two SPIs (18 Mbit/s, 4-bit to 16-bit frames); SWD.

STM32F030x4, x6 and x8 are value-line Cortex-M0 microcontrollers running to 48 MHz, with 16 KB to 64 KB of flash and 4 KB or 8 KB of SRAM, in TSSOP20, LQFP32, LQFP48 and LQFP64. They all work from 2.4 V to 3.6 V at -40 °C to 85 °C ambient. The x8 parts add TIM6, TIM15, SPI2, USART2 and I2C2.

SRAM runs at the CPU clock with no wait states and has hardware parity that raises an exception on an error. Option bytes write-protect flash in 4 KB blocks and set readout protection: level 0 none; level 1 blocks flash reads and writes while a debugger is attached or the chip has booted from RAM; level 2 disables the SWD debug port and boot from RAM altogether.
At reset the BOOT0 pin and a boot option bit select user flash, system memory or SRAM. System memory holds the factory boot loader, which reprograms the flash over a USART on PA14/PA15 or PA9/PA10.
Computes a CRC-32 (the Ethernet polynomial) over 32-bit words, for example to check a flash signature at run time against one stored at link time (an EN/IEC 60335-1 measure).

VDD (2.4 V to 3.6 V) feeds the I/O and the internal regulator; VDDA (2.4 V to 3.6 V) feeds the ADC, the reset circuits, the RC oscillators and the PLL. VDDA has to be at least VDD and present first. As an absolute maximum, VDD may sit above VDDA by 0.4 V at most. Every supply and ground pin is connected.

Power-on and power-down reset are always on and hold the chip in reset below VPOR/PDR (1.88 V falling, 1.92 V rising, typical) with no external part. The power-on detector watches VDD only; the power-down detector watches VDD and VDDA, and its VDDA half can be switched off with an option bit to save current when VDDA is known never to fall below VDD. The reset temporization tRSTTEMPO is 1.5 ms to 4.5 ms.

The internal regulator makes the 1.8 V core supply. Its main mode serves Run; a low-power mode may be used in Stop; in Standby it is off with a high-impedance output, so the core loses its registers and SRAM. It is always on after reset.
Only the CPU stops; peripherals keep running and any interrupt or event wakes it, in about 1.1 µs.

Every clock in the 1.8 V domain stops and the PLL, HSI and HSE are off, but SRAM and registers keep their contents; the regulator stays in main or low-power mode. Any EXTI line wakes it, whether the RTC alarm or any of the 16 external lines. Wakeup takes about 4.2 µs with the regulator in run mode.

The regulator is off and the whole 1.8 V domain is unpowered, as are the PLL, HSI and HSE; only the standby circuitry keeps its state; SRAM and registers are lost. It ends on NRST, an IWDG reset, an RTC alarm or a WKUP pin going high. The RTC, the IWDG and their clocks keep running in Stop and Standby.

The chip starts on the internal 8 MHz RC (HSI). A 4 MHz to 32 MHz crystal or external clock (HSE) can take over; it is watched by the clock security system, which falls back to the HSI and can raise an interrupt if the HSE fails. The PLL multiplies HSI/2 or HSE (divided 1 to 16) by 2 to 16, up to 48 MHz. AHB and APB run to 48 MHz each. A separate 14 MHz RC (HSI14) clocks the ADC; a 40 kHz RC (LSI) clocks the IWDG and can clock the RTC. MCO outputs a chosen clock on PA8.
The RTC runs from a 32.768 kHz crystal (LSE), a resonator or oscillator, the 40 kHz LSI, or HSE divided by 32. On the STM32F030x8 the MCO output cannot select LSI or LSE.

Each pin can be an input (floating, pull-up or pull-down), a push-pull or open-drain output, or an alternate function; most share digital or analog peripherals. A locking sequence freezes a port's configuration. All pins are floating inputs during and after reset except where noted (SWDIO and SWCLK). Up to 55 I/Os, up to 36 of them 5 V tolerant.

An input left at a middle voltage draws current through its Schmitt trigger, and a floating input can drift or toggle with noise. Set unused pins and ADC inputs to analog mode, or tie them to a level with a pull resistor or by making them outputs.

A GPIO sinks or sources up to 8 mA within the normal VOL/VOH, and up to 20 mA with relaxed levels (1.3 V). The total sourced current plus the chip's own run current must stay within ΣIVDD (120 mA), and the sunk total within ΣIVSS. PC13, PC14 and PC15 sit behind the backup power switch: only 3 mA, at most 2 MHz into 30 pF, never as a current source.

Five channels move data between memory and peripherals in either direction, or from memory to memory, with circular buffers, independent source and destination sizes, and a software trigger on each channel. SPI, I2C, USART, ADC and every timer except TIM14 can use it.

The NVIC takes up to 32 maskable channels (besides the 16 core lines) at 4 priority levels, with tail-chaining and automatic state saving. The EXTI has 24 edge-detector lines, each set for rising, falling or both edges and masked on its own; it catches pulses narrower than one internal clock period. The 16 external lines take any of up to 55 GPIOs.

One 12-bit successive-approximation ADC, 1 µs per conversion at 14 MHz, with up to 16 external channels plus the temperature sensor (ADC_IN16) and VREFINT (ADC_IN17); single or scan conversion, DMA, and an analog watchdog that interrupts when a channel leaves a window. It converts 0 V to VDDA. Calibrate it after each power-up.

Gives a voltage that rises linearly with temperature, about 4.3 mV/°C and 1.43 V at 25 °C. The offset differs from chip to chip, so uncalibrated it only suits detecting changes; the two factory readings TS_CAL1 (30 °C) and TS_CAL2 (110 °C) at VDDA = 3.3 V correct it.
VREFINT, a bandgap of about 1.2 V, is on ADC_IN17; its factory reading at 30 °C and VDDA = 3.3 V is VREFINT_CAL.

TIM1 is a 16-bit advanced timer: four channels, three with complementary outputs and programmable dead time, a break input, edge or centre-aligned PWM and one-pulse mode, usable as a three-phase PWM. TIM3 is a 16-bit up/down timer with four channels that also decodes quadrature encoders and 1 to 3 Hall sensors. TIM14 has one channel; TIM15 two; TIM16 and TIM17 one each with a complementary output and dead time. TIM6 is a basic time base. Timers can be chained (timer link), and every counter can be frozen while debugging. TIM16 and TIM17 each have a modulator gate for IR control (IR_OUT); TIM3 suits decoding IR remote signals.

The IWDG has an 8-bit prescaler and a 12-bit down-counter clocked by the LSI, so it runs in Stop and Standby; it is started by hardware or software as the option bytes choose. The WWDG is a 7-bit down-counter on PCLK with an early-warning interrupt. SysTick is a 24-bit auto-reload down-counter on HCLK or HCLK/8.

A BCD calendar with sub-seconds, seconds to years and automatic month-length and leap-year handling; an alarm and periodic wakeup that bring the chip out of Stop or Standby; smooth correction of 1 to 32767 clock pulses and digital calibration in 1 ppm steps; two tamper pins with filters and a timestamp input, both able to wake the chip; and a 50 Hz or 60 Hz reference input (RTC_REFIN) to refine the calendar.

Up to two interfaces, master or slave, at 100 kbit/s and 400 kbit/s; I2C1 also does Fast-mode Plus at 1 Mbit/s with 20 mA drive on the FTf pins, and SMBus 2.0/PMBus 1.1 (ARP, host notify, PEC, timeouts, ALERT). Both have 7-bit and 10-bit addressing, two slave addresses (one with a mask), analog and digital noise filters and DMA. The pins are not true open-drain: in open-drain mode the PMOS to VDD is off but still there.

Up to two, at up to 6 Mbit/s, with CTS/RTS flow control, multiprocessor mode, synchronous master mode and single-wire half duplex. USART1 adds auto baud detection and the receiver timeout. Both work with DMA.
Up to two, master or slave, full or half duplex, to 18 Mbit/s; frames of 4 to 16 bits, eight master baud rates, hardware CRC, Rx/Tx FIFOs, NSS pulse mode and TI mode.
Serial wire debug on PA13 (SWDIO) and PA14 (SWCLK).
PB2 and PB8 are not available on the LQFP32 and no hardware drives them to a defined level there; they are treated as unconnected pins.

Use a 4 MHz to 32 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator, mounted with its load capacitors as close to OSC_IN and OSC_OUT as possible to cut distortion and start-up time. CL1 and CL2, usually equal, are high-quality ceramics of 5 pF to 20 pF; their series value plus about 10 pF of pin and board capacitance should match the crystal's load figure. Start-up takes about 2 ms at 8 MHz. ST application note AN2867 covers crystal choice.

A 32.768 kHz crystal with its load capacitors close to OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT; no resistor may go between the two pins. Four drive levels (LSEDRV) trade 0.5 µA to 1.4 µA of current for transconductance. Start-up takes about 2 s.
NRST has a permanent pull-up of about 40 kΩ, a Schmitt input with about 200 mV hysteresis, and a filter that ignores pulses under 100 ns; a pulse of 300 ns or more always resets.

Software should detect and recover from a corrupted program counter, unexpected resets and corrupted control registers. Most such failures can be reproduced by holding NRST or an oscillator pin low for one second; ESD on the chip then shows what the software must survive (ST application note AN1015).

Voltages refer to VSS. Min and max figures hold over the full temperature, supply and frequency range and are tested on every part at 25 °C and TAmax; figures marked as from characterization are mean ± 3σ of samples. Typical figures are at 25 °C and VDD = VDDA = 3.3 V. Pin figures are measured into 50 pF. Run-mode currents use code equivalent to CoreMark, with flash wait states set for the clock (none to 24 MHz, one above).

At TAmax = 82 °C, IDDmax = 50 mA and VDD = 3.5 V, with 20 outputs low at 8 mA (0.4 V) and 8 low at 20 mA (1.3 V): PINT = 175 mW, PI/O = 272 mW, PD = 447 mW, and on the LQFP64 (45 °C/W) TJ = 102.1 °C, inside the suffix 6 limit of 105 °C. A second case at 100 °C ambient, 20 mA and 20 outputs at 8 mA gives PD = 134 mW and TJ = 106.03 °C, over the suffix 6 limit. The power derating curve shows PD falling to zero at 105 °C for suffix 6 and 125 °C for suffix 7; suffix 7 parts are found in the STM32F05x line.
